sources.exact_short_claim: not among the modern Yucatec Mayas
sources.source_restriction: The discontinuity sentence cites Villa Rojas (1945) and is background framing in a cognition/gesture study, not a complete 2026 Yucatan community calendar census; field sites are two named communities. Local continuous use cannot be asserted or universally denied.
sources.source_predicate: The old 260-day calendar is historically discussed; these contemporary communities' timekeeping uses Gregorian and agricultural/religious cycles, not demonstrated uninterrupted natal named-day count.

arithmetic.source_justification: Existing fixed lowland correlation and one-day hypothetical Sacred rollover; these are not 4 observed Yucatec daykeeper practices.
arithmetic.conceptual_implication: As long as all four source/date policies are equally possible, not even one civil date has a CHUWEN-positive classification that is invariant across all four; do not require this invariance to *test a declared reconstruction*.
arithmetic.baseline_selector_not_permitted: After-response choice of offset/correlation is model fitting and invalidates untouched validation.

method_protocol_status.outcome_condition: One prospective declared model can be tested if ethical source-construct and analysis freeze is complete even if historical local continuity remains unknown; disclosure must be honest that it is a reconstruction.

outside_scope: Do not make a negative statement about all living Yucatec communities based on two field sites or Villa Rojas 1945.
